prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create one wide 4-panel editorial watercolor and fine-pencil storyboard for an academic museum interaction design. Muted sage, terracotta, indigo, warm ivory. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos. Four consistent panels left to right showing only the tabletop, hands and a forearm with an ordinary plain sleeve cuff, not a face or whole person. Panel 1: at an accessible small table, a sleeve cuff rests inside a clearly outlined small rectangular capture zone on a neutral mat beneath a document camera. A small reference card shows a generic invented abstract textile detail, distinctly not a real historical artwork. A plain tote-bag corner on the table edge indicates an alternative target but stays outside the capture zone. Panel 2: the same cuff in the same capture zone and a nearby monitor displaying the unmodified generic source thumbnail, a close cropped cuff photo, and an illustrative AI-generated motif design on that cuff. No body or face on monitor. Panel 3: hands deliberately fold back the same cuff, making one physical change inside the capture zone, and press one simple unlabelled button beside the mat. Panel 4: monitor shows before and after close cropped cuff designs side by side, with the folded cuff visible on the table and a hand pointing to a changed line. The original fabric remains physically plain in every panel, all added motifs appear only in clearly screen-framed digital previews. The source thumbnail remains unchanged. Simple practical camera and screen, no robotics, no projection, no VR. Clean clear hands with correct anatomy. Keep everything inside generous margins and separators. Show the small local capture area, action and visual response clearly. This is a proposed design illustration, not a real deployment or a photograph, and the motif is an invented placeholder.
scope: Current cuff-or-bag concept storyboard. Invented reference patterns. Other diagrams are original SVG layout sketches.
